Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xxs / timeouts from rw-11b in production

Rachel / Neha —

Investigating. Early signal summary:
- Between 08:40–09:00 PT we observe a correlated spike in gRPC 5xxs and request timeouts from fraction of rw-11b pods in us-west-2.
- Errors originate at the serving runtime (stack traces point to a kernel fallback path when certain attention tile sizes hit a quantization boundary).
- Model-ops: there is an open perf regressed quantization kernel deployed with rw-11b:v2 that can amplify tail latency under the request-length distribution NW is hitting.

Immediate actions taken (10:00 PT):
- Enabled aggressive request shedding on affected pods to reduce overload (will cause some requests to fail fast).
- Scoped traffic: temporarily routed 30% of NW traffic to rw-11b:stable-legacy (non-quant) as an intermediate mitigation.
- Kicked a rolling restart for the small subset of failing hosts.

Remaining asks / risks:
- Full rollback of rw-11b:v2 quant kernel requires a short maintenance window and will briefly reduce capacity.
- Fallback to rw-10b will reduce quality for some prompts; propose routing critical endpoints only.

I'll prepare a short mitigation plan and ETA within the hour. Attaching log extract and early metric charts.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rw-11b-log-sample.txt (same), rw11b-metrics-10-03.png (image, 45KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@northwind.io>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: rw-11b incident: root cause, mitigation & temporary routing plan

Hi Liam / NorthWind team —

Thanks for your patience. Below is what we have so far and the actions we’ve taken.

Root cause (preliminary):
- A regression in a quantization-optimized kernel introduced in rw-11b:v2 causes occasional attention-kernel slow paths when inputs exceed certain token-layout thresholds. Under specific request-length distributions (which NorthWind’s endpoints exercise), this produced long-tail CPU/GPU stalls and subsequent 5xx/timeouts.

Mitigation already applied (11:00 PT):
- 30% of traffic routed to rw-11b:stable-legacy (non-quantized) — immediate reduction in 5xx rate by ~60% for affected endpoints.
- Rolling restart of ~12% of affected serving hosts to clear kernel state.
- Temporary request-shedding policy to fail fast for very long requests (to prevent cascading overload).

Planned next steps & ETA:
- 11 Apr 12:30 PT: Deploy rollback of the quantization kernel for rw-11b:v2 to remove regressed path (estimated 20–30 minute maintenance, may incur brief capacity reduction).
- 11 Apr 13:00 PT: Monitor for stabilization for 6 hours; if stable, we will gradually reopen full traffic.
- 12 Apr: Postmortem draft (root cause + remediation + test coverage) shared with NW for review.

Workarounds for NorthWind (recommended):
- If you have critical endpoints, we can route 100% of those to rw-10b or rw-11b:stable-legacy during the window. Expect minor quality delta for some prompts.
- Reduce max-request-length or enforce prefix caching on long sequences where feasible to lower incidence of the slow path.

What Redwood will provide:
- Real-time updates in this thread every hour during mitigation window.
- Post-incident postmortem with timeline, fixes, and code-path tests.
- A one-off service credit proposal for impact window.

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.md (text), rw11b-rollback-plan.patch

Subject: rw-11b incident: resolution summary and next steps (postmortem attached)

Hi Liam / Sanjay —

Following up with a resolution summary. Thanks again for working with us while we resolved the rw-11b elevated 5xxs/timeouts.

What happened (short):
- A quantization kernel regression in rw-11b:v2 caused sporadic long-tail stalls under NorthWind’s request distribution, leading to elevated 5xxs and timeouts across a subset of pods (we observed peak impact on 2027-04-11 08:45–09:30 PT).

What we did:
- Rolled back the regressed quant kernel (11 Apr 12:30 PT).
- Scoped traffic routing and rolling restarts to remove affected hosts.
- Implemented additional runtime checks to prevent the specific fallback path from engaging in production without a gating performance test.
- Shipped updates to our CI test coverage to include token-layout distributions that replicate NW workload.

Current state:
- Full stabilization verified as of 2027-04-13 16:20 PT across our us-west-2 fleet.
- Error rates for your impacted endpoints returned to baseline (<0.1% 5xx) and 95th percentile latency dropped to pre-incident numbers.

What we will share next:
- Draft postmortem (attached) for your review with timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation.
- A short runbook update and the acceptance tests we added to CI.
- A proposed service credit for the impact window — Neha will coordinate.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute review with Marcus and model-ops to walk through the technical details and answer any questions.

Next immediate ask for NorthWind: please confirm whether you want the critical endpoints fully routed to rw-10b for the next 48 hours while we continue monitoring, or if you prefer to stay on the default routing now that stabilization is confirmed.

Apologies again for the disruption. We value your partnership and will follow up with the finalized postmortem (we included an internal action list and ETA for each item).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
